olivia (support): FYI escalated from @raj — customer sees TypeScript + bundler resolution problems with our node SDK in a Next.js SSR build. They also get intermittent 401s after bundling. Repro steps below.

raj (customer): repro: next 13.4 + pnpm 8 + node 18.14. When I import our SDK in API routes it works locally, but after build+deploy to Vercel I get 401s from the API and TS errors during build: 

  ERROR in ./pages/api/chat.ts:
  Module not found: Can't resolve 'redwood-inference'
  
and during tsc: 
  TS7016: Could not find a declaration file for module 'redwood-inference'.

I narrowed it to our package exports map — bundler picks the ESM entry but the runtime expects CJS alt for native node fetch handling. Also noticed esbuild rewrites auth header on serverless edge build? :confused:

olivia (support): Thanks — can you paste package.json `exports` and the import line you use? Also your deploy logs showing 401s (curl to our hosted API) would be helpful.

raj (customer): import is `import { Redwood } from 'redwood-inference'`
package.json snippet:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/index.cjs",
    "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```

Deploy log (trim):
`[edge-runtime] POST /api/chat -> 401 Unauthorized (token missing)`
Locally same request has Authorization header present. After build the header is dropped by bundler/edge shim.

olivia (support): Got it. tagging eng: @todd and devx: @kim for packaging/bundler context. Sounds like two linked issues: (1) TS types not being picked up from `types` path for some bundlers, (2) conditional export choice causing an ESM-only build which Vercel edge runtime transforms and strips headers.

kim (devx): quick thoughts — Vercel/Turbopack/esbuild sometimes prefer the `import` entry and tree-shake server-only code. If our ESM build uses `globalThis.fetch` vs `node:fetch` differences, the edge shim may inline and drop node headers. Also TypeScript resolution for `types` under `exports` can be flaky pre-TS 4.9.

Workarounds to try:
1) explicit import of CJS path: `const { Redwood } = require('redwood-inference/dist/index.cjs')` or `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference/dist/index.mjs'` depending on runtime.
2) pin Node version and disable edge runtime (use nodejs serverless instead of edge) to confirm header stripping.
3) add a `exports` fallthrough default: "default": "./dist/index.cjs" so bundlers that don't support conditional exports pick a CJS entry.

Would like packaging team to propose a long-term fix. @todd can you triage?

packaging-bot: New issue created: RW-ops/packaging#842 — "conditional exports/types: Next/Vercel SSR build + auth header drop and types not found". Labels: p1, packaging, nextjs, esbuild.

todd (eng): Thanks @olivia @kim. Repro notes/questions:
- Which SDK version? (raj: 1.4.2)
- Do you use `exports` exactly as pasted or any additional fields?
- Can you share `next.config.js` and whether you target `experimental.edge` or `server`?

raj (customer): SDK 1.4.2, next.config has `experimental: { runtime: 'edge' }` for the API routes. We tried switching to `node` runtime and the 401s stopped — header preserved. TS error still happens at build unless I add `skipLibCheck` or manually add `types` paths in tsconfig.

todd (eng): Good signal — edge runtime seems to trigger header issue due to ESM path. Plan:
- Short term: publish a patch 1.4.3 that adds "default": "./dist/index.cjs" and ships a small wrapper `dist/index.node.cjs` that explicitly exports CommonJS for node and includes a bundled types file. Also add a note in README about edge runtimes requiring explicit CJS import or node runtime.
- Medium: update build to ensure our ESM output uses stable `node:` imports and that auth headers are forwarded by runtime adapters; add tests for Vercel/Turbopack.

kim (devx): For the TS side, we'll also publish an @types/shim or ensure `types` key in exports points to a top-level `index.d.ts` that TS can pick up when `typesVersions` fallback fails. I'll add a CI job that runs `pnpm dlx create-next-app` + build against package to catch regressions.

raj (customer): thanks — can you patch me the test build? I can verify on my project.

todd (eng): Will cut 1.4.3-rc.1 today with the `default` export and CJS wrapper. @olivia please share the RC link to raj. Also adding regression test and issue owner.

olivia (support): Sending RC now: https://artifact.pkg/1.4.3-rc.1 — raj please try with `npm i redwood-inference@1.4.3-rc.1` and report back.

raj (customer): Installed and deployed — looks good, headers preserved and no 401s. TS build still gives one warning but resolves with `skipLibCheck: false` (I can paste if needed).

todd (eng): re: TS warning — tracked in RW-ops/packaging#843, will ship types-only patch. Closing P1 for auth drop; keeping packaging issue open for types. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

olivia (support): Marking resolved for the immediate customer auth/401 issue. Leaving thread for packaging follow-up.

packaging-bot: Issue RW-ops/packaging#842 updated: status -> in_progress; assigned -> todd.
